(1) JOIN STRATEGY (Q2 FAIL fix) — NEW LEADING CANONICAL block in resources/24-trino-cbo-analyze.md inserted BEFORE §1 (between the existing 'Two pasteable rules' callout and the '## 1. Teaches the three Trino 467 levers (verified against trino.io/docs/current/optimizer/cost-based-optimizations.html): (i) PRIMARY — `SET SESSION join_distribution_type = 'PARTITIONED'` / 'BROADCAST' / 'AUTOMATIC' — the direct on/off switch (three accepted values, default AUTOMATIC, session-scoped); (ii) SECONDARY — `SET SESSION join_max_broadcast_table_size = '50MB'` (default 100MB) — the AUTOMATIC-mode broadcast threshold; (iii) TERTIARY — bare `ANALYZE iceberg.analytics.events` to populate NDV stats so CBO chooses correctly. EXPLAIN (TYPE DISTRIBUTED) verification block included. DO-NOT-WRITE matrix bans 6 forbidden hint forms verbatim with inline correction: `/*+ USE_HASH_JOIN(a,b) */` (Oracle hint syntax), `/*+ USE_PARTITIONED_JOIN(a,b) */` (Spark/Hive-influenced naming), `/*+ BROADCAST(small_dim) */` (Spark hint name), `/*+ MAPJOIN(small_dim) */` (Hive hint name), `/*+ DISTRIBUTION_TYPE(PARTITIONED) */` (plausible-looking guess), any `/*+ ANY_HINT_NAME(...) */` — all silently treated as block comment per trinodb/trino #9498 (open FR, not implemented in 467/481). Silent-wrong failure-mode callout included (worse than parse error — no feedback). (2) TO_CHAR / DATE FORMATTING (Q4 FAIL fix) — NEW LEADING CANONICAL block in resources/27-oracle-plsql-to-dbt-trino.md inserted at the top of §4.2 (Date/time functions), BEFORE the existing Oracle→Trino table: '### LEADING CANONICAL — Oracle `TO_CHAR(date, fmt)` → Trino'. Teaches the two canonical Trino 467 functions verified against trino.io/docs/current/functions/datetime.html: (i) `date_format(timestamp, format)` — MySQL-style specifiers (`%Y`, `%m`, `%d`, `%H`, `%i`, `%s`) — FIRST-CHOICE; (ii) `format_datetime(timestamp, pattern)` — Joda DateTime pattern (`yyyy`, `MM`, `dd`, `HH`, `mm`, `ss`) — equivalent. 3-line worked example (Oracle TO_CHAR → both Trino forms). Plain-ISO `CAST(d AS VARCHAR)` fallback callout (works only for plain-ISO output of a DATE/TIMESTAMP column). 13-row Oracle TO_CHAR mask ↔ Trino MySQL-pattern ↔ Trino Joda-pattern mapping table covering the patterns engineers migrate most often (`'YYYY-MM-DD'`, `'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'`, `'DD/MM/YYYY'`, `'MM/DD/YYYY'`, `'Mon DD, YYYY'`, `'Month DD, YYYY'`, `'HH24:MI'`, `'HH24:MI:SS'`, `'YYYY'`, `'MM'`, `'DD'`, `'D'`, `'WW'`, `'Q'`). 4 pattern-grammar pitfalls explicitly called out (MySQL `%Y` 4-digit-year vs `%y` 2-digit; Joda `MM`-month vs `mm`-minute; MySQL `%i`-minute vs `%M`-month-name; 24-clock `%H`/`HH` vs 12-clock `%h`/`hh`). Niche `format('%1$td...', ts)` Java Formatter syntax labelled as niche-only fallback. DO-NOT-WRITE matrix bans 6 forbidden forms verbatim with inline correction: `TO_CHAR(order_ts, 'YYYY-MM-DD')` (Oracle, Function 'to_char' not registered), `CAST(order_ts AS DATE)::VARCHAR` (PostgreSQL/Snowflake/DuckDB `::` operator — Trino has none per trinodb/trino #23795, open FR, not in 467/481), `order_ts::VARCHAR` / any `expr::type`, calling `::` 'syntactic sugar for CAST' (misconception), `STR_TO_DATE` (MySQL), `CONVERT(VARCHAR, ts, 23)` (SQL Server style codes). Meta-rule: 'in Trino, use Trino's dialect — Oracle/PostgreSQL/Snowflake/Spark/SQL-Server function names and operators that look idiomatic in other engines parse-error or function-not-registered against Trino 467.' ALSO updated the existing TO_CHAR row in the inline §4.2 translation table (was: `format_datetime` only; now: `date_format` FIRST-CHOICE + cross-reference to LEADING CANONICAL).

(3) CONSOLIDATED CROSS-DIALECT GUARDRAIL — NEW §4.4B 'CROSS-DIALECT-SPILLOVER GUARDRAIL — syntax that looks valid but is NOT Trino 467' inserted in r27 right after §4.4A (the existing cast-syntax guardrail). 13-row consolidated table mapping every recurring cross-dialect spillover: cast operator (`::` → `CAST`), query hints (`/*+ ... */` → `SET SESSION`), QUALIFY (Snowflake/BigQuery → ROW_NUMBER subquery), `ANALYZE TABLE` (Spark/Hive → bare `ANALYZE`), `TO_CHAR` (Oracle → `date_format`/`format_datetime`), `STR_TO_DATE` (MySQL → `date_parse`/`parse_datetime`), `NVL`/`NVL2` (Oracle → `COALESCE`/`CASE WHEN`), DECODE-with-NULL (Oracle → searched CASE), `ROWNUM` (Oracle → `LIMIT`), Iceberg compression key (`write.parquet.compression-codec` → `compression_codec`), Iceberg WITH-clause shape (`properties = map(...)` → flat name=value pairs), Spark TBLPROPERTIES (`SET TBLPROPERTIES('k'='v')` → `SET PROPERTIES k='v'`), Iceberg snapshot timestamp (`timestamp_ms` → `committed_at`). Closing meta-rule: 'when unsure, prefer ANSI / standard SQL forms (`CAST(... AS ...)`, `COALESCE`, `CASE WHEN`) and SESSION properties (`SET SESSION ...`); do not paste PostgreSQL / Oracle / Snowflake / Spark / native-Iceberg idioms into Trino.' WEBSEARCH VERIFICATION:
- Trino `join_distribution_type` session property: three accepted values AUTOMATIC (default), PARTITIONED, BROADCAST; verified via trino.io/docs/current/optimizer/cost-based-optimizations.html and trino.io/docs/current/admin/properties-general.html.
- Trino `join_max_broadcast_table_size` default 100MB; same source.
- Trino has NO query-hint syntax; `/*+ ... */` parsed as block comment; open FR trinodb/trino issue #9498 (not implemented in 467/481).
- Trino `::` cast operator NOT supported; open FR trinodb/trino issue #23795 (not implemented in 467/481).
- Trino `date_format(timestamp, format)` uses MySQL-style format specifiers (compatible with MySQL `date_parse`/`str_to_date`); verified via trino.io/docs/current/functions/datetime.html.
- Trino `format_datetime(timestamp, pattern)` uses Joda DateTime pattern format; same source.
- Pattern-specifier conventions (MySQL `%Y` 4-digit year, `%m` zero-padded month, `%H` 24-hour, `%i` minute, `%s` second; Joda `yyyy` 4-digit year, `MM` zero-padded month, `HH` 24-hour, `mm` minute, `ss` second) verified via same source.
